reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Digoxin clearly reached its pharmacokinetic target (serum drug concentration was measured). The nomogram arm achieved a mean SDC of 0.52 ng/ml and 86.2% achieved SDC < 1.0 ng/ml, demonstrating the nomogram successfully lowered concentrations compared to standard dosing (mean 1.12 ng/ml, 42.4% < 1.0 ng/ml). The drug was administered and absorbed — target engagement at the Na+/K+-ATPase is assumed given measurable serum concentrations. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The trial did not measure downstream pharmacodynamic markers (inotropy, heart rate) directly. SDC is a PK surrogate, not a PD biomarker of Na+/K+-ATPase inhibition or downstream biology. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving SDC 0.5–0.9 ng/ml. The nomogram arm achieved 38.5% vs 34.8% in standard care — both arms failed to achieve the target concentration range in the majority of patients. The nomogram did shift concentrations lower (mean 0.52 vs 1.12 ng/ml) and improved safety (more patients below 1.0 ng/ml), but the narrow therapeutic window target (0.5–0.9 ng/ml) was not reliably achieved by either strategy. This is fundamentally a dosing/delivery precision failure — the nomogram could not reliably place patients in the narrow target range. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: ABCB1 pharmacogenetic subgroups showed only modest variation in SDC in the nomogram arm, suggesting pharmacogenetic factors were not a major driver of the failure. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial enrolled 131 patients over 3 years. No p-value was reported, suggesting the comparison may not have been formally powered for statistical inference on the primary endpoint. The failure appears to be a dosing precision/delivery issue — the nomogram algorithm itself was insufficient to reliably achieve the narrow 0.5–0.9 ng/ml window, even though it successfully reduced concentrations below 1.0 ng/ml. This is a manufacturing/delivery (dosing algorithm) failure rather than a mechanistic failure of digoxin itself.

failure_modes.evidence: The nomogram dosing algorithm failed to reliably place patients in the target SDC range of 0.5–0.9 ng/ml (only 38.5% achieved this), despite successfully reducing mean SDC to 0.52 ng/ml and getting 86.2% below 1.0 ng/ml. The failure is in the precision of the dosing algorithm, not in the drug's mechanism or biology.

Heart failure patients have variable pharmacokinetics (renal function, body composition, drug interactions) that may make a simplified nomogram based on creatinine clearance and ideal body weight insufficient to achieve a narrow therapeutic window in a heterogeneous population.

The failure mode sits at the intersection of 'manufacturing_or_delivery' (dosing algorithm imprecision) and trial design (the narrow 0.5–0.9 ng/ml window may be inherently difficult to achieve in a heterogeneous population).
